title: Whiteman, Perez Prado, Dizzy, Armstrong and Parker
summary: He re-recorded Rhapsody in Blue, played Prado's solo, and recorded with Dizzy, Armstrong and Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: And then, of course, Paul Whiteman. He went with another company, so I got to make the "Rhapsody in Blue" with him all over again. And that was a big kick for me. And as I
No, the Mexican band leader made it, Ruby Red or whatever -- "Cherry Red?"
Perez Prado, yes, came in from Mexico and I did a lot of dates with him, and he recorded that trumpet solo that was famous, so I got to make that trumpet solo with him.
Did you get to do that?
That was on RCA, wasn't it?

Yes, I think you were. And we made "Emaline" , another tune like that. And I made some records -- well, I made a lot of albums with Dizzy because he didn't have any set big band, of course. And I made quite a few albums with his band. And in the '40s I got to make a record with Louis Armstrong, who was always my big idol. "Fish Market Blues" with Roy Eldridge, that record. I even made an album with Charlie Parker. They had a big band, all the strings and everything.
